_about: Compliance knowledge base for children's tableware. A rule applies when every condition in 'applies' matches: products / materials / features are any-of lists (omitted = all), and max_age_months means the rule applies when the youngest intended user is younger than that. NOT LEGAL ADVICE: regulations change. Confirm every item with an accredited test lab or compliance consultant before launch.

rules.title: Children's Product Certificate (CPC) based on third-party testing
rules.requirement: Products designed primarily for children 12 and under need a CPC issued by the importer or domestic manufacturer, based on tests by a CPSC-accepted third-party lab, covering every applicable children's product safety rule.
rules.evidence: CPC document + test reports from a CPSC-accepted lab; periodic testing plan.

rules.title: Permanent tracking labels on product and packaging
rules.requirement: Permanent distinguishing marks on the product and its packaging (to the extent practicable): manufacturer/private labeller, location and date of production, batch/run information.
rules.evidence: Label artwork showing mould-in or printed tracking information.

rules.title: Total lead in accessible substrate ≤ 100 ppm
rules.requirement: Every accessible component material must contain no more than 100 ppm total lead.
rules.evidence: Third-party lab test per component material / colour.

rules.title: Lead in paint and surface coatings ≤ 90 ppm
rules.requirement: Paints, inks and surface coatings must not exceed 90 ppm lead.
rules.evidence: Third-party lab test of each ink/coating colour.

rules.title: Phthalates (child care articles) ≤ 0.1% each
rules.requirement: Products that help children 3 and younger with feeding are 'child care articles'. Accessible plasticised parts must not contain more than 0.1% of each of 8 restricted phthalates (DEHP, DBP, BBP, DINP, DIBP, DPENP, DHEXP, DCHP).
rules.evidence: Third-party test, unless the material qualifies for a determination in 16 CFR 1308 (e.g. certain unplasticised plastics). Confirm with your lab.

rules.title: Small parts: no detachable parts that fit the small-parts cylinder
rules.requirement: Articles intended for children under 3 must not have, or release after use-and-abuse testing, parts that fit the small parts cylinder. Check suction cups, valves, lids, spouts, decorative pieces and silicone tips that can be bitten off.
rules.evidence: Use-and-abuse + small parts test report (16 CFR 1500.51-53).

rules.title: Sharp edges and points
rules.requirement: No accessible sharp edges or points, before or after use-and-abuse testing. This matters especially for metal cutlery, fork tines and breakage points.
rules.evidence: Sharp edge / point test (16 CFR 1500.48-49).

rules.title: Food-contact materials permitted by FDA
rules.requirement: Every food-contact material and additive must be permitted for its intended use and temperature (food additive regulation, GRAS, prior sanction or Food Contact Notification).
rules.evidence: Supplier letters of guaranty / compliance statements naming the 21 CFR section; migration tests if needed.

rules.title: Silicone: rubber articles for repeated use
rules.requirement: Silicone for repeated food contact is typically covered by 21 CFR 177.2600, including its extractives limits (water and n-hexane).
rules.evidence: 21 CFR 177.2600 extraction test report; supplier statement.

rules.title: Polyolefins (PP/PE)
rules.requirement: The resin grade must meet 21 CFR 177.1520 (olefin polymers) for its intended use conditions, and colourants must be permitted (21 CFR 178.3297).
rules.evidence: Resin and masterbatch supplier FDA compliance letters.

rules.title: Melamine: no microwave use, heat limits
rules.requirement: Melamine-formaldehyde (21 CFR 177.1460) is permitted, but FDA advises against microwaving food in melamine because melamine/formaldehyde migration increases with heat. 'Bamboo' melamine composites are still melamine and shouldn't be marketed as natural.
rules.evidence: Migration test at intended temperature; 'not for microwave' labelling.
rules.reference: 21 CFR 177.1460; FDA consumer guidance on melamine

rules.title: Leachable lead & cadmium in ceramicware
rules.requirement: Glazed ceramics and decorated glass must meet FDA leachable lead and cadmium action levels. Cups, mugs and children's items have the strictest limits.
rules.evidence: Leach test (e.g. ASTM C738) per glaze/decoration.

rules.title: California Proposition 65
rules.requirement: A clear warning is needed if exposure to a listed chemical (e.g. lead, BPA, certain phthalates) is above the safe-harbour level. Most brands avoid this through material controls rather than warnings.
rules.evidence: Test screening for listed chemicals; supplier declarations.

rules.title: State laws on chemicals in children's products (incl. PFAS)
rules.requirement: Several states restrict or require reporting of chemicals in children's products, including intentionally added PFAS bans in children's/juvenile products (e.g. WA, OR, VT, ME, MN, NY and others). Requirements and dates differ by state.
rules.evidence: Supplier PFAS-free declarations; state reporting where required.
rules.reference: e.g. WA Children's Safe Products Act; OR Toxic-Free Kids Act; MN Amara's Law; VT Act 131

rules.title: Button/coin battery requirements (Reese's Law)
rules.requirement: Battery compartments must be secured and meet performance tests, with warnings on product, packaging and instructions.
rules.evidence: 16 CFR 1263 test report; warning artwork.

rules.title: Framework Regulation for food-contact materials
rules.requirement: Materials must not transfer constituents to food in quantities that endanger health or change the food unacceptably. Products need traceability and 'for food contact' wording or the glass-and-fork symbol (unless obviously intended for food).
rules.evidence: Risk assessment; traceability system; labelling.

rules.title: Good manufacturing practice for food-contact materials
rules.requirement: Documented quality assurance and quality control at every stage of manufacture.
rules.evidence: GMP documentation from the factory.

rules.title: Plastics Regulation: Union list, migration limits, Declaration of Compliance
rules.requirement: Only authorised monomers and additives may be used. The article must meet overall migration (10 mg/dm², or 60 mg/kg for articles for infants and young children) and specific migration limits, and a written Declaration of Compliance must be passed down the supply chain.
rules.evidence: Declaration of Compliance (DoC); overall and specific migration tests with the right simulants and temperatures.

rules.title: STOP: bamboo/plant-fibre plastic composites not authorised
rules.requirement: Bamboo powder, wood flour and similar fibres aren't authorised additives under 10/2011, and EU enforcement campaigns have removed these products from the market. Redesign with an authorised material.
rules.evidence: Don't launch this material in the EU.

rules.title: BPA and hazardous bisphenols banned in food-contact materials
rules.requirement: BPA and other hazardous bisphenols are banned in food-contact plastics, coatings, varnishes, inks, adhesives, rubbers and ion-exchange resins, with transitional periods. Polycarbonate products and epoxy-coated items are affected.
rules.evidence: Supplier declarations; avoid polycarbonate / epoxy coatings.

rules.title: Silicone: national rules (no specific EU measure)
rules.requirement: Silicone has no harmonised EU measure, so it must still meet 1935/2004 Art. 3. Retailers and authorities commonly expect testing to German BfR Recommendation XV (incl. volatile organic compounds ≤ 0.5%) and LFGB, or French rules for the French market.
rules.evidence: BfR XV / LFGB test report incl. VOC content and migration.

rules.title: Metals and alloys (stainless steel)
rules.requirement: Metals have no harmonised measure. The Council of Europe technical guide sets specific release limits (e.g. Ni, Cr); some member states have national rules.
rules.evidence: Metal release test per CoE guide; steel grade certificate.
rules.reference: Council of Europe Resolution CM/Res(2013)9 and technical guide

rules.title: Ceramics: lead and cadmium migration
rules.requirement: Lead and cadmium migration limits for ceramic articles apply (the directive is being revised towards lower limits and more metals).
rules.evidence: Pb/Cd migration test.

rules.title: Import controls for melamine kitchenware from China / Hong Kong
rules.requirement: Imports need a declaration and lab report showing compliance with formaldehyde and melamine migration limits, with prior notification at the point of entry.
rules.evidence: Lab report + declaration per consignment.

rules.title: EN 14372 - cutlery and feeding utensils
rules.requirement: This is the European safety standard for children's cutlery and feeding utensils: mechanical hazards (small parts, sharp edges, strength) and chemical requirements (e.g. phthalates, migration). It's widely expected by retailers and market surveillance.
rules.evidence: EN 14372 test report.

rules.title: EN 14350 - drinking equipment
rules.requirement: This is the European safety standard for children's drinking equipment (cups, spouts, valves, straws): mechanical, chemical and information requirements.
rules.evidence: EN 14350 test report.

rules.title: General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR)
rules.requirement: Requires an internal risk assessment and technical documentation, an EU-based responsible economic operator, a product identifier (type/batch), manufacturer name and postal and electronic address on the product or packaging, safety information in local languages, matching information on online listings, and accident reporting via Safety Business Gateway.
rules.evidence: Technical file; label artwork; online listing info.

rules.title: REACH Annex XVII: phthalates & PAHs in childcare articles
rules.requirement: Childcare articles (incl. feeding) must not contain restricted phthalates above 0.1% (entries 51/52). Rubber/plastic parts in direct, prolonged or repeated skin or mouth contact must not exceed PAH limits (entry 50).
rules.evidence: Phthalate + PAH test report.

rules.title: SVHC Candidate List communication + SCIP
rules.requirement: If any article contains a Candidate List substance above 0.1% w/w, you must give customers safe-use information (Art. 33) and notify the SCIP database.
rules.evidence: SVHC screening test or supplier declarations, updated each Candidate List revision.
rules.reference: REACH Art. 33; Waste Framework Directive Art. 9

rules.title: Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)
rules.requirement: New EU-wide packaging rules apply in phases from August 2026: restrictions on PFAS in food-contact packaging, packaging minimisation and recyclability requirements, and harmonised sorting labels phased in later.
rules.evidence: Packaging specification; supplier declarations.

rules.title: Electronics: Batteries Regulation, RED/EMC, RoHS, WEEE, button-cell safety
rules.requirement: Products with electronics bring CE marking (EMC/RED/RoHS), WEEE registration, Batteries Regulation labelling and removability rules, and secure battery compartments.
rules.evidence: CE technical file; DoC.

rules.title: Food-contact materials (retained EU law)
rules.requirement: The UK versions of 1935/2004, 2023/2006 and, for plastics, 10/2011 apply, with separate legislation for England, Wales, Scotland and NI (NI follows EU rules). Bamboo-fibre plastics are treated as non-compliant (FSA).
rules.evidence: DoC referencing UK legislation; migration tests.
rules.reference: Materials and Articles in Contact with Food (England) Regulations 2012; Plastic Materials and Articles in Contact with Food (England) Regulations 2009

rules.title: General product safety (UK)
rules.requirement: Products must be safe, with producer identification and traceability. Northern Ireland follows EU GPSR. Watch secondary legislation under the Product Regulation and Metrology Act 2025.
rules.evidence: Risk assessment; technical file; label artwork with UK address.
rules.reference: General Product Safety Regulations 2005; Product Regulation and Metrology Act 2025

rules.title: BS EN 14372 / BS EN 14350
rules.requirement: UK retailers expect the same European standards for feeding utensils and drinking equipment.
rules.evidence: Test reports.

rules.title: UK REACH restrictions (phthalates, PAHs) and SVHC duties
rules.requirement: UK REACH Annex 17 restrictions and candidate-list communication duties mirror EU REACH as retained.
rules.evidence: Same test reports as EU REACH.

rules.title: Canada Consumer Product Safety Act
rules.requirement: General prohibition on products that pose a danger to health or safety, mandatory incident reporting within the required timelines, and record-keeping for traceability.
rules.evidence: Risk assessment; incident reporting procedure; supply-chain records.

rules.title: Phthalates Regulations (child care articles)
rules.requirement: Vinyl in child care articles (which includes feeding articles for children under 4) is restricted to ≤ 1000 mg/kg of DEHP, DBP and BBP, and of DINP, DIDP and DnOP where the part can be placed in the mouth.
rules.evidence: Phthalate test of any vinyl/plasticised part.

rules.title: Lead in consumer products that may be mouthed by children
rules.requirement: Accessible parts of products that children may put in their mouths must not exceed 90 mg/kg total lead.
rules.evidence: Total lead test per material.
rules.reference: Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations SOR/2018-83

rules.title: Food and Drugs Act - food packaging and contact materials
rules.requirement: Contact materials must not transfer harmful substances to food. A Health Canada Letter of No Objection is optional but often requested by retailers.
rules.evidence: FDA/EU compliance evidence usually accepted; LONO if a retailer requires it.
rules.reference: Food and Drugs Act s.4; Food and Drug Regulations B.23.001

rules.title: Glazed ceramics and glassware lead/cadmium leach limits
rules.requirement: Leachable lead and cadmium limits apply to glazed ceramics and glassware for food.
rules.evidence: Leach test report.
rules.reference: Glazed Ceramics and Glassware Regulations SOR/2016-175

rules.title: Bilingual labelling
rules.requirement: Required consumer information on pre-packaged products must be in English and French (plus Quebec Charter of the French Language rules).
rules.evidence: Packaging artwork.
rules.reference: Consumer Packaging and Labelling Act; Quebec Charter of the French Language

rules.title: Australian Consumer Law: general safety duty and mandatory reporting
rules.requirement: Suppliers must report (within 2 days) any death, serious injury or illness associated with their product, and have recall procedures in place. A general safety provision applies under the ACL.
rules.evidence: Incident reporting procedure; risk assessment.
rules.reference: Competition and Consumer Act 2010 Sch 2 (ACL) s.131

rules.title: Food contact materials must not contaminate food
rules.requirement: Food businesses must not use materials likely to cause food contamination. There are no specific positive lists, so brands generally show compliance with EU 10/2011 or US FDA rules plus AS 2070 (plastics for food contact).
rules.evidence: EU/FDA test evidence; AS 2070 if requested.

rules.title: Button/coin battery mandatory standards
rules.requirement: Secure battery compartments, compliance testing, warnings and packaging requirements apply.
rules.evidence: Test report to the mandatory standard; warning artwork.
rules.reference: Consumer Goods (Products Containing Button/Coin Batteries) Safety Standard 2020

rules.title: Substantiate dishwasher resistance
rules.requirement: Test colour fastness, print adhesion, warping and (for silicone) odour/stain after repeated dishwasher cycles, and test suction cups and valves after the cycles too.
rules.evidence: EN 12875 test (e.g. 125 or 500 cycles) or equivalent.

rules.title: Substantiate microwave suitability
rules.requirement: Run migration tests at microwave conditions (food simulant + temperature) and check warping/heat build-up. Never claim this for melamine or bamboo composites; for metal, it's not applicable.
rules.evidence: Migration test at high temperature; heating test.
rules.reference: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex V (test conditions); 21 CFR 176.170(c) Table 2

rules.title: Suction performance + hygiene validation
rules.requirement: Define and test a pull-off force on smooth, textured and wooden highchair trays, with release-tab usability for adults. Check water-trap and mould risk under the suction base, and confirm it can be cleaned (disassembly or open design). These are the top complaint drivers in this category.
rules.evidence: Internal test protocol; user testing log; cleaning validation.

rules.title: Hot-water chamber: scald and leak risk
rules.requirement: Check that the plug/valve can't be removed by a child, leak testing at temperature, and surface temperature limits.
rules.evidence: Leak + surface temperature tests; child-resistant plug evaluation.
